body.x: Korean ICT companies with outstanding technology participated in “CES 2016”, the world’s largest IT and electronics exhibition. They received positive reviews from buyers worldwide, including those from the U.S., and established a bridgehead for advancing into foreign markets.
(Picture description: Foreign buyers at the joint pavilion prepared by Daegu TP MTCC at CES 2016)

According to the Mobile Technology Convergence Center of Daegu TP, 16 regional organizations and 27 domestic companies accomplished great achievements at the joint pavilion, signing various contracts and MOUs with other companies.
In particular, the companies succeeded in garnering attention from foreign buyers by arranging their products strategically -- all according to the selected technology themes at the joint pavilion.
Among participating companies, RNWARE, U-HANPRESEN, Quantumgames, and 3.14 obtained solid results.
(Picture description: Buyers listening to product explanations at the booths of RNWARE (left) and U-HANPRESEN (right))

RNWARE showcased the smart wireless transmission device “ANYSYNC Full HD” at this CES. This is a wireless device that can transmit in real time images and audio of various devices -- including smartphones, tablets, PCs, and camcorders -- to external output devices, such as TVs and beam projectors.
At the event, the company signed a $68,000 sales contract with a Belgian company whose name begins with A. In the future, it will expand its exports to Europe, Indonesia, Japan, and China.
U-HANPRESEN’s “Presenmarker” is a solution that can draw lines, shapes, and letters on an image projected by a projector. It can also save presentations as video files by using a mouse.

The company signed an MOU for technical cooperation and exports with a Turkish project company whose name begins with P. Furthermore, the company is invited to Taiwan to discuss export contracts in February by OPTOMA, the No. 1 company in the DLP projector market.
(Picture description: Buyers looking at products and technologies at the booths of Quantumgames (left) and 3.14 (right))
Quantumgames, a startup, showcased its “Screen Baseball System”, which enables one to enjoy baseball games realistically even in an indoor setting. It utilizes a projector and sensor technology.

The company garnered much attention, as the LA Dodgers and a Major League Baseball player from the Cincinnati Reds visited the booth. The product received favorable reviews in that it is more than just a sensory content -- it can also be used by professional athletes. The company will continue to put much effort into developing the screen baseball system.

After showcasing its “KamiBot”, a moving paper toy, 3.14 received much attention from American toy distribution franchises and school officials. It is also discussing additional contracts in Silicon Valley.

Daegu Mayor Kwon Young-jin said: “We have participated in CES for four years in order to help venture and small and medium-sized companies -- all with outstanding technology in the ICT convergence field -- enter foreign markets and earn export contracts.”

“As they have gained more confidence in their technical skills in the global market, we will prepare various support plans for advancing into foreign markets. We will try our best to support them, so they can contribute to the realization of a creative economy.”
